comment: How a seat's turn is run. The role comes from policy/library.json (lane -> role); each library role runs as the custom agent profile `<profilePrefix><role>` (install them with `npm run harness -- agents install`) unless `agents` maps it to another; generated roles run as `<profilePrefix><fallback.agent>` with their charter in the prompt. A profile that isn't installed is skipped (no --agent) rather than failing the turn; the other CLIs get the profile's text as standing instructions. `models` maps the library's model placeholders to what runs them: empty for Copilot's default model, a Copilot model id, or `<cli>:<model>` to run those seats in another CLI: `claude:opus`, `codex:<model>`, `pi:<provider/model>`, `omp:<model>` (`<cli>:` alone for that CLI's default). Some Copilot plans offer one model and refuse --model, so the judges' placeholder (model-b) goes to Claude by default: judges on the same model as the work they judge share its blind spots. Copilot tool flags come from the seat's catalog permissions through `tools` and `always`; a seat without a write permission also gets --deny-tool write. `cli` does the same for each other CLI, keyed by catalog permission (`repo:write:lease` stands for every repo:write:*): claude takes tool names as in --allowedTools, with `deny` and `noWrite`; codex takes -c settings (`config` for every turn, `windowsConfig` on Windows) and its sandbox follows the write permission, and `userProvider` keeps the model provider and default model from your own Codex config (the rest of that config is never loaded; an inline token is passed in an environment variable); pi and omp take tool names (`read`, `write`, `shell`, extra `tools`) and `commands`, the shell commands the turn gate lets through (`always` for every seat, "git diff *" for a prefix). `worker`: run every seat that does the work as one worker agent (profile af-worker) given its lane's skill, instead of a role per lane; judges keep their roles. `sessions`: "todo" or "goal" carries the worker's CLI session across turns of a todo or goal (Copilot and pi; judges always start fresh). `worker` is on: on Copilot it scored 0.99 against 0.96 for a role per lane (eval full-copilot-2, 2026-10-31), and it never did worse. `sessions` stays off: todos finish in about one turn, so it made no difference, and a goal-wide session cost Codex about two thirds more tokens. `lanes` applies only when the policy has no team.
